content: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. If the situation is not life-threatening, contact a poison control center without delay. Residents in the United States can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, it is essential to undergo laboratory and/or medical tests, such as liver and kidney function tests, viral load assessments, and T-cell counts, to monitor your health. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. For 10-milligram tablets, keep them in their original container along with the drying agent (desiccant) provided. Ensure the bottle is tightly closed when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific needs. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for comprehensive information about this product and your individual health requirements. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not cover all potential drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist.
